title: Decent app with a few “frustrations”
body:

Came in particularly useful when I had a serious illness and went into physical rehab as I had my baseline / pre-illness info and could track my rehab progress. The heart rate alerts was an early warning for a cardiac issue that was confirmed later on by drs.

Units can be in metric or imperial 

Biggest Frustration:- 
1- does NOT automatically track or detect when starting or completing an outdoor walk. Particularly frustrating when I’ve completed a walk then driven home & it tracks the whole journey, including the car drive as a walk, even when I use Apple Maps to navigate the drive 

2- does not allow edits to the above e.g. No one can walk or run at 50 - 100kmh but I can’t delete that portion out of my journey

3- does not allow me to add customised activity e.g. gardening, housework

4- Cannot edit or delete the splits or legs where a drive in a car was recorded during an outdoor walk

I absolutely love Apple Fitness+.

One thing I’d love to see is an Apple Fitness+ “Wrapped” style recap at the end of the year — something shareable that celebrates streaks, workouts completed, favourite trainers, awards and milestones. It would be great motivation for users and great promotion for the app.

I also wish Apple made a bigger deal of major milestones, especially a full-year exercise streak. Hitting 52 weeks felt huge, but the app didn’t really celebrate it.

Overall, I love the app. It helped me start small, stay consistent, and build real momentum.

title: Game changer - love this app
body:
Update on the app - one year later and I renewing my annual subscription as I am still using and loving this app - I can level up or down and focus on different parts of my body depending on what I’m training for. Right now, it’s core and toning as I prepare my bikini beach body for Hawaii. Brilliant! 

That said, I’ve downgraded to 4 stars as there are a few tips the team might consider:
- being Australian, it would be useful to include metric weights and measurements (every time, not just sometimes) 
- please add the focus of the set in the title (eg not just ‘mindful cool-down with Greg’ but ‘upper body cool-down’ or ‘whole body cool-down’ etc so you don’t have to waste time clicking and opening til you find something suitable - useful for all mat, hiit and strength workouts
 - add a ‘routine’ page so you can save a weekly routine of your choice of classes so you don’t have to search each time you return to workout. Right now, I’m working on a bunch of classes on alternate days and it’s annoying to have to scroll to find them every time I come back to exercise. 

Simple and effective changes will improve the user experience. 

Thanks team - you have helped me get fit again, I am truly grateful! 

——
2022
As someone who had been fit and active but had prolonged inactivity forced upon me after an injury, this app has been perfect for motivating me to get active again. Closing the move, exercise and activity rings every day has been a game changer. My fitness level has been all but restored within three months - I have lost the extra weight I gained, I can literally see my muscle rebuilding where it had wasted away, my heart health has improved, my step count tripled and I have so much more energy each day. I trialled the free version when I purchased my Apple Watch - I thought, why not, 3 months free, what was there to lose? I’d just started going to a personal trainer after recovering from an injury and a series of surgeries, but he was about to have a holiday so I was left to my own devices. The app gave me the convenience of guided exercise whenever I wanted, rather than having to get in the car to go to the gym and motivate myself. It has so many exercise options and new sets to choose from with different trainers each week. Yes, looking at other reviews, there are definitely things I’d improve (eg intuitive starts and pauses to walking/running, more sensitivity to stand function which sometimes fails to register). Please, app designers, please work these frustrations out - surely it can be done. Despite its shortfalls, I’m giving it a 5 star review because it has been the single most effective app I have ever used - it pulled me out of a two-year funk and has supported me to be restored to a fitness level I never thought I’d enjoy again. It’s not a silver bullet, but it is good for people who are determined to put disciplines into their life, and willing to make the changes in lifestyle. I put my tv away, put reminders in my calendar to kickstart my new routines and make this work. I’m SO glad I did, I feel ten years younger.

title: Fitness App Disappeared from iPad Pro
body:
Have Apple One Premier subscription. 
Updated iPad Pro to iPadOS 16.3. 
Apple Fitness+ App disappeared from Home Screen, and not present in App Library. However, searching the App Store I can still locate the Fitness app, but can’t download it only open it.

Workaround one: view and use Fitness videos one my iPhone. 

Workaround two: search App Store (doesn’t appear in App Library at all) for Apple Fitness, open the app. 

Workaround three: completely turn off screen time (not ideal for families with children). Fitness app comes back. Note, screen time settings were not changed before the update, and the Fitness app is and has always been allowed in ‘Allowed Apps’. It seems that there is a bug in the latest update which is linked to Apple Fitness and Screen Time on iPad. iPhone is unaffected.  

Workaround four: downgrade subscription, don’t use Apple Fitness.

Two stars because there has been so many past problems accessing the app, and I have spend many hours trouble shooting this issue for myself, family and friends. I expect more reliable service when paying such an expensive subscription price coupled with an expensive device. 

Note: content within the app is good. Delivery of consistent and reliable service for this app is very poor. Fitness is highlighted as a key component of Apple One Premier. Thus the lack of availability and reliability of the Fitness app tarnishes the appeal, value and experience of Apple One and and the service of Apple overall.   

When it comes to fitness activities and meditation people want to ‘just do it’. We don’t want to suddenly and unexpectedly be trouble shooting a missing app and trying to understand why. The why is the responsibility of Apple and its engineers. Apple customers pay very good money for very good products, and the expectation of a very good experience.

title: Superb
body:

So easy to use. Great variety and instructors. Safe and gimmick free. Doesn’t proclaim to save the world.

For all the people complaining that it “isn’t or doesn’t have something” - it doesn’t need it. 

Consistency and basic, safe, make you puff a bit, exercise is all you need. There is no magic pill. There is no magic exercise. The basics and your own motivation is all you need. 

Thank you Apple for making it so easy and inexpensive.

title: Fitness App
body:
This app seems best suited to under 40s running round urban streets. It is not well adapted to many of the daily activities of older people.
Heavy duty pick, shovel and wheelbarrow work over half days doesn’t register as exercise. Walking the dog may or may not be recognised. Pushing a lawnmower registers, but not for all the time. Strenuous axe work, chopping wood for heating, tends to provoke great alarm, and questions plural as to whether I’ve had a fall. On occasion it has had to be prevented from making emergency phone calls when there was no emergency, just a more than usually tough log. It’s all a bit frustrating and there’s no way to get rid of it or go to a more laidback persona. 
This app would benefit from a capacity to work a personality change and a capacity to tell it once and once only that the impact it has just registered isn’t a dangerous fall.

title: Please fix this Apple

title: Really?
body:
I really only use this for tracking walking and general light exercise, for the most part it’s fine (dammed by faint praise) but there a couple of things that are needlessly frustrating. 

1. I’m based in Australia and like most of the world, we’re metric. The app on my iPhone gives me stats like feet and inches per kilometre (how is that useful?). The Apple Watch ignores my metric setting to give only miles and calories. What more do I need to do to sort this out?

2. On the Apple Watch the Workout app (yes, linked but not the same app) seems incapable of working out when I have paused. Surely for a non performance based general walk or run there could be a setting that automatically figures that out? So, if I pause and forget to unpause both Activity and the Workout appear to discount anything I did during that time.
